A: Maya has been offered the lead role on an Antarctic climate expedition, a career-making appointment requiring eight months away. Her brother is recovering from a difficult divorce and depends on their weekly dinners, while her elderly father expects her help at home. Should Maya accept the expedition or remain close to her family this year?
B: A second-division goalkeeper can join a top club if he moves abroad before preseason. The contract could finally establish his professional career, but he would miss his daughter's first year of school and leave the neighborhood team he has trained with since childhood. Should he sign abroad or keep playing near the people who rely on him?
C: While checking telescope images, Priya discovers that her longtime lab partner altered several measurements in their joint paper. Reporting the changes would protect the scientific record but could end his career and expose a friend who once defended her during a misconduct inquiry. Should Priya alert the journal or give her partner a chance to avoid public consequences?

A: Jonah's cycling results have earned him a place at a national training academy two cities away. Moving there could put him on the Olympic development squad, yet it would end his daily rides with his father and remove him from the amateur club where his closest friends gather. Should Jonah relocate for elite training or stay with his community team?
B: After years teaching evening classes, Elena is invited to direct a prestigious graduate program in another country. The post offers research funding and a clear path to a deanship, but her mother, siblings, and close colleagues all live nearby and share childcare each week. Should Elena pursue the appointment or preserve the life they have built together?
C: A village football club has played every home match on natural grass for ninety years, maintained by generations of volunteers. A grant would replace it with artificial turf, allowing winter games and cheaper upkeep, but former players say the old pitch anchors the club's identity. Should the committee install the new surface or preserve the traditional field?

A: Dr. Chen can become chief surgeon by transferring to the hospital's distant flagship campus. The promotion would bring authority, better cases, and recognition after years of training, but her spouse cannot relocate and their twin sons have just settled into school. Should she take the leadership post or remain with her family and current team?
B: Omar, a city planner, has been chosen to oversee a nationally visible rail expansion in the capital. Accepting would accelerate his career, yet his partner runs a local shop and his closest friends depend on their standing Sunday gatherings after several hard years. Should Omar move for the project or remain rooted in the city they share?
C: A clinic receptionist has saved enough to replace the failing boiler in her flat before winter. A regular patient arrives unable to pay for insulin until payday and faces several dangerous days without it. Covering the prescription would delay the repair and leave her own home unreliable. Should she protect her savings or buy the patient's medication?

A: Leah is offered command of a regional fire brigade, a promotion she has pursued for a decade. The role requires relocating and remaining on call most weekends, when she currently coaches her niece and cooks for her extended family. Should Leah accept the command and advance, or keep the routines that hold her close relationships together?
B: Rafi's neighborhood bakery has attracted an investor who will finance three new locations if he moves downtown to manage expansion. Growth could make his reputation and secure the business, but his wife and cousins operate the original shop together and fear losing their daily bond. Should Rafi chase the larger enterprise or stay alongside the family crew?
C: During a water-quality inspection, Tomas finds that his former academy roommate, now a plant supervisor, omitted a failed test from the municipal log. Correcting the record may trigger discipline and public anger against his friend, while silence leaves residents with false information. Should Tomas file the accurate report or protect the person who helped him begin his career?

A: Nadia founded a neighborhood garden that now occupies most evenings with friends and relatives. A national nonprofit offers her a paid fellowship to replicate it across twenty cities, but the travel would make her largely absent from the original garden and its tight volunteer circle. Should Nadia scale her work nationally or remain present with the group that built it?
B: A marine biologist receives funding to run her own laboratory on an island research station. The appointment could establish her as a leading coral expert, but it means leaving her partner and the colleagues who have shared her fieldwork for six years. Should she depart for an independent scientific career or keep her place within her existing relationships?
C: To win residents' trust for a youth shelter, Malik considers telling the planning committee that he lived in temporary housing as a teenager. The disclosure could explain his commitment and unlock cooperation, but the experience is private and several neighbors know his family. Should Malik share that history publicly or keep it confidential despite the project's stalled support?

A: Dev has set aside his freelance income for three months of rent after losing a major software client. His former intern calls because her laptop died before a paid coding assessment, and she cannot afford another. Lending her his backup machine risks delaying his own work and income. Should Dev keep the equipment available or help her take the assessment?
B: A substitute teacher has saved a small emergency fund after months of irregular shifts. One pupil's father asks her to cover the fee for a required exam because an unexpected eviction consumed the family's cash. Paying would let the student graduate, but leave the teacher unable to handle her own next missed paycheck. Should she retain the fund or pay his fee?
C: A startup can let volunteers install experimental plug-ins in its coding platform, encouraging unexpected tools and discoveries. Security staff warn that an unreviewed plug-in could corrupt users' projects, while mandatory approval would make every extension predictable but restrict experimentation. Should the team open the platform to independent plug-ins or require a protected, reviewed catalog?

A: Inez has reserved the proceeds from two paintings to repair her studio roof before the rainy season. A cellist in her shared building needs urgent dental treatment and cannot perform while in pain. Paying the bill would help him return to work but expose her canvases to another month of leaks. Should Inez fund his treatment or protect her studio savings?
B: A nurse keeps a modest cash reserve because her hospital contract may not be renewed. Her widowed neighbor, whom she checks on weekly, needs a hearing aid to understand medical appointments but cannot cover the deposit. Buying it would consume most of the reserve. Should the nurse preserve her financial cushion or help her neighbor hear essential instructions?
C: Sofia wants to stage her first gallery show with unsettling sculptures made from discarded appliances. Her parents and fellow artists promise to attend only if she exhibits the gentle landscape paintings for which they know her. The sculptures feel more honest, but an empty opening could damage those relationships. Should Sofia present her preferred work or choose the paintings that secure their approval?

A: Marcus has budgeted his remaining scholarship money for textbooks and meals through the semester. His classmate, who has been sleeping in a car, asks for help with a hostel deposit after the campus shelter fills. Paying could give her a safe week indoors but force Marcus to skip required books. Should he keep the money for school or cover her room?
B: The owner of a repair shop has enough cash either to replace a failing compressor or to help his only mechanic after her apartment burns. Without the machine, the shop may lose jobs and threaten his livelihood; without a deposit, she and her son remain in a motel. Should he secure the equipment or use the money to house his employee?
C: A private tutoring company can double its margin by replacing reusable workbooks with cheap single-use packets mailed to every student each week. The switch would raise the owner's income, but thousands of coated pages and plastic sleeves would be discarded monthly. Should she adopt the profitable packets or accept lower earnings to reduce the waste imposed on others?

A: A dairy farmer has stored enough feed to carry his herd through a forecast dry month. His neighbor's injured horse has gone without proper hay, and she cannot buy more until insurance pays. Sharing the feed would relieve the animal now but could leave his own cattle short. Should the farmer keep his full reserve or give her several bales?
B: Residents saved donations to repair the roof of their volunteer hall before autumn storms. A longtime volunteer needs a wheelchair ramp at home after an accident, and no public grant will arrive for months. Redirecting the fund would postpone the roof and risk water damage. Should the committee protect the hall budget or build the ramp for him now?
C: A young farmer can plant an unfamiliar heritage grain that may command a premium and reveal which crops suit the changing climate. Her insurer will cover only the standard wheat with predictable yields, which would protect the farm if summer turns harsh. Should she experiment with the untested grain or choose the insured crop and a safer harvest?

A: Lena has kept the final month's reserve needed to cover rent at her struggling cafe. Her dishwasher reveals that his child needs a specialist appointment requiring immediate payment, which he cannot raise. Giving him an advance may prevent the appointment from being canceled but could leave the cafe unable to open. Should Lena preserve the reserve or advance his wages?
B: A theater costume designer has saved enough to replace the sewing machine that repeatedly stalls before deadlines. Her longtime stagehand needs money for a train ticket to reach his hospitalized sister tonight. Buying the ticket could reunite them, but another machine failure may cost the designer her next contract. Should she keep the replacement fund or pay his fare?
C: A bookstore charges every stallholder the same nonrefundable fee for its annual makers' fair. One ceramic artist misses the cancellation deadline because she was caring for her injured son and asks for her money back. Refunding her would ease a real hardship but break the rule applied to three others. Should the owner enforce the fee or grant her an exception?

A: After recurring migraines, a geologist is told to spend two quiet days away from screens and fieldwork. That weekend she is scheduled to calibrate sensors for a colleague's only permitted glacier flight, and no trained replacement is available. Canceling would waste his limited research window. Should she rest as advised or fulfill her commitment despite the likely pain?
B: A farmer strains his back just before the cooperative's shared irrigation channel must be cleared. The doctor recommends a week without lifting, but his assigned section blocks water from reaching four neighboring plots and every other farmer is already working upstream. Should he protect his recovery or complete the clearing he promised before the crops dry out?
C: Each evening, a doctoral student plans to spend ninety focused minutes reviewing statistics before her qualifying exam in six months. Her friends now gather downstairs for relaxed dinners and films after work, and joining them would make a lonely winter far more pleasant. Should she maintain the demanding study routine for future mastery or enjoy the easy evenings with them?

A: A rowing coach develops bronchitis days before the junior crew's regional final. Her physician orders rest because cold mornings may prolong the illness, yet the inexperienced substitute has never guided this crew through a race and the athletes have trained under her all year. Should she stay home to recover or coach the team as she promised?
B: Eli twisted his ankle while carrying supplies for the neighborhood food pantry. He is due to coordinate Saturday's distribution to sixty families, but the clinic says standing all day could delay healing, and the only backup volunteer is unfamiliar with the records. Should Eli protect his ankle or run the distribution others are counting on?
C: A local running club promised residents a new riverside route map before Sunday's charity race. Publishing Friday would give volunteers time to mark the course, but two distances remain unverified and errors could send runners onto traffic-heavy streets. Should the cartographer release the map on schedule or delay it until every segment has been checked carefully?
